The *Sirimittattheragāthā* (Thag 8.2) is a canonical poem in the *Theragāthā* collection, preserving verses attributed to the elder Sirimitta [SuttaCentral]. Modern translations listed on SuttaCentral include renderings in eight languages, featuring an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral]. The text is cited or mentioned in later Pali canonical and para-canonical works, including the *Peṭakopadesa* (Pe 3, *Suttādhiṭṭhānatatiyabhūmi*) and the *Therāpadāna* (Tha-Ap 65, *Paccāgamaniyattheraapadāna*) [SuttaCentral].

SuttaCentral notes verse parallels in non-Pali Buddhist literature, notably the Gāndhārī Dharmapada (G3-Dhp 1–10) and the Patna Dharmapada (P-Dhp 327–341, *Dadantīvagga*), as well as canonical Pali parallels in the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 4.52, AN 5.47, AN 7.5, AN 7.6, and AN 7.7) and the *Saṁyutta Nikāya* (SN 11.14 and SN 55.26) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus corroborates these alignments, finding shared Pali passages between segments 7.2–8.5 and the *Sattakanipāta* (AN 7.6), segments 6.1–8.5 and the *Sotāpatti Saṁyutta* (SN 55.26), as well as substantial textual overlap across segments 1.1–8.5 in the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* and matches in the *Saṅgāyana-puccha vissajjanā* [DharmaNexus].
